  historical label; the three keys are real and present in today's seed (`image`,

readFirst.text: PROGRAM SETUP — Meal Planner app registered on the tm control plane. program/ scaffolded in the main checkout; CONTRACT.md drafted as a BUILD contract (repo-state vs installed-state denominators, running-app-as-instrument, >=2 comparators) and is NOT frozen — T0.1 verifies and freezes it. CLAUDE.md router created at the project root with the kit fence. Execution is sequential: seed.json, the running meal-server, and the shared markdown library are global mutable state.

PRODUCTION SYNC SERVER IS DOWN — and it is down in a way that looks up. The launchd job
com.mealplanner.server (pid 89492, running since 25 Jul) still HOLDS port 8765, but every
request fails: GET /index.html -> 404, GET /sw.js -> 404, GET /sync.json -> 500
("build_seed.py returned non-zero exit status 2"). The same meal-server.py started from a
shell session on port 8766 serves all three at 200, from the same files, so this is the
LaunchAgent's environment and not the code. SYNC-SETUP.md predicts exactly this cause:
/usr/bin/python3 needs Full Disk Access to read anything under ~/Documents, and a
LaunchAgent does not inherit Terminal's grant. The doc says the agent then "crash-loops
silently" — it does not. It stays up and serves errors, which is why nothing surfaced it.
Last successful sync was 2026-08-01 08:52 (mtime of app/seed.json and app/.thumb-cache.json,
both server-written). tailscale serve still proxies the phone's https URL to 127.0.0.1:8765,
so the phone's Sync has been failing since then; an installed phone still works offline off
its service-worker cache, but a FRESH install cannot load the app shell at all.

What this means for other tasks: CONTRACT §3's "the running app" instrument is NOT the
launchd server. Any task making a behavior claim must start its own instance
(MEAL_PORT=8766 MP_BASE_DIR=... python3 meal-server.py) and say so. Do not read a green
port as a green server: deploy.sh only checks that something LISTENS on 8765, so it would
print "Server is up" over this exact failure. Fixing the LaunchAgent is a user action
(System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Full Disk Access -> add /usr/bin/python3); it is
not in T0.1's scope and has not been done.

THE CLAUDE-SIDE SKILLS ARE ON THIS FILESYSTEM AND READABLE — STATE.md's open question is
answered, and Wave 1 is unblocked. All five (recipe-capture, meal-planner, grocery-list,
inventory, cook-feedback) live as SKILL.md files in the desktop app's extracted read-only
plugin cache. Find the path rather than hardcoding it, because it contains session UUIDs:

  find ~/Library/Application\ Support/Claude -type d -name recipe-capture 2>/dev/null

Today that resolves to .../local-agent-mode-sessions/<session>/<sub>/rpm/
plugin_015FwuR4F4oA8McKxoM2JgGP/skills/. Plugin manifest: name "meal-planning", version
0.2.0, extracted 2026-07-03. A second identical copy sits under Claude-Account2 (verified
byte-identical with diff -rq).

Read-only is the operative word. The plugin's SOURCE of record is not on this filesystem
— only this extracted snapshot plus the hand-authored replacements the user keeps in
"Meal planning/plugin-updates/" (SKILL.md for meal-planner, grocery-list, inventory,
cook-feedback — but NOT recipe-capture, which has never been revised there). So Wave 1's
deliverable shape is confirmed, not merely predicted: T1.1/T1.2 ship a SKILL.md patch
spec plus a user install step (Settings -> Capabilities), per plugin-updates/
README-INSTALL.md. The 2026-08-03 loop-def LOG entry called this correctly.

One naming caveat for T1.1: the seed is at schemaVersion 3, not 2 (inventory-sync landed
after the Phase-2 note in ROADMAP.md). The three keys T1.1 targets are real and present in
the built seed today — recipe objects carry image, thawHoursAhead, prepAhead — so T1.1's
substance stands; only its "schemaVersion-2" label is historical. Do not go hunting for a
v2 seed to match.

CORRECTION TO ENTRY #4 — THE SERVER IS FIXED, AND MY DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. Entry #4 said the
launchd server's 404/500 was caused by /usr/bin/python3 lacking Full Disk Access. That is
refuted. While cleaning up my own test server I ran an over-broad pkill -f "meal-server.py"
that also killed the launchd process (pid 89492, up since 25 Jul); launchd restarted it at
14:08:33, and the fresh process serves everything correctly: 200 on /index.html, /sw.js,
/js/pwa.js, /manifest.webmanifest, /icon-192.png, and 1,087,727 bytes on /sync.json —
including through tailscale on the phone's own HTTPS URL. Same LaunchAgent, same plist, same
interpreter. So Full Disk Access is granted and always was; a missing grant cannot be the
cause. The kill was unintended (I meant to stop only my own instance on 8766) and I am
reporting it as such, not as a repair I planned.

What survives from #4, all still measured: the old process served 404 on every static path
and 500 on /sync.json for days WHILE HOLDING THE PORT; a listening port is therefore not
evidence of a working server, and deploy.sh's lsof-LISTEN health check would have printed
its success tick over it (T0.2 fixes that). Last known-good sync before the outage was
2026-08-01 08:52.

What is now unknown: why a long-running process lost the ability to read under ~/Documents
while a fresh one has no trouble. Candidates nobody has tested — a TCC grant re-evaluated
against an already-running process, an OS update (host is Darwin 25.3.0) invalidating the
running process's authorization, or a firmlink/volume change under the path. Do not repeat
the FDA story as the cause. If the outage recurs, capture evidence BEFORE restarting: the
restart is the thing that destroys the only specimen.

Practical rule, unchanged in effect: curl a real path before trusting any server, and if the
launchd one is answering 404s, `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.mealplanner.server`
is now a known-working remedy.

state.settledDecisionsMd:
- **Keyless & private.** No API key ships in the app. In-app conversational planning was
  built, then removed for security; the Mac-mini + Tailscale bridge replaced it. Not
  reopened without the user.
- **Planning is conversational; execution is the app.** Recipe and plan *generation* lives
  in the Claude skills; the app assembles from the library and never authors it.
- **Sync is one-way pull + a feedback push.** Live two-way sync (ROADMAP #8) is explicitly
  deferred and out of scope for every current wave.
- **Design system is "Sage", dark-first, borderless hairline rows** (`DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`).
  Settled — extend it, don't revisit it.
- **Execution is sequential** (README §Execution model): `seed.json`, the running server,
  and the shared markdown library are global mutable state. *T0.1 refinement:* the contended
  resource is the **port**, not the code — `build_seed.py` writes to the invoking checkout and
  `.thumb-cache.json` is per-checkout, so a worktree run with `MP_BASE_DIR` set writes nothing
  shared (CONTRACT §10).
- **`app/seed.json` is server-owned runtime output**, not a source file awaiting a commit.
  `meal-server.py` rewrites it on every `/sync.json` request, so the main checkout is
  permanently dirty and `deploy.sh` refuses by construction. Never `git add -A`.
state.openQuestionsMd:
- ~~Where do the Claude-side meal-planning skills live on disk?~~ **Settled by T0.1:** all
  five are readable at the desktop plugin's extracted cache (`meal-planning` v0.2.0); none is
  writable. Wave 1 ships a SKILL.md patch spec + a user install step. LOG #5 has the `find`.
- ~~Does the repo-state / installed-state split describe what a phone experiences?~~
  **Settled by T0.1: no** — it was too coarse. CONTRACT §1 now defines four states, because
  data reaches the phone through `/sync.json` on every sync while the app shell reaches it only
  through a hand-bumped `const CACHE`.
- **Why did a long-running `meal-server.py` lose the ability to read under `~/Documents`,
  while a fresh one has no trouble?** Open and unexplained. Full Disk Access is ruled out.
  Untested candidates: a TCC grant re-evaluated against an already-running process, an OS
  update (Darwin 25.3.0) invalidating a running process's authorization, a firmlink change
  under the path. Whoever sees it next: capture evidence **before** restarting.
- At 3–4 weeks, what does "week 2 mirrors from the freezer" become? Genuine design
  question, not a loop bound. (T2.1)
- Has the in-app "Heads up" card actually fallen short in real use? Wave 3's gate depends
  on it, and only the user can answer. (T3.1)
state.authoritativeMd:
Established by T0.1 (`findings/T0.1.md`), measured on the library as of 2026-08-04.

- **Library:** 35 recipes · 304 ingredients · 5 meal plans · 98 plan entries · 71 purchase
  units · 20 pantry items · 52 cookbook photos. `seed.json` = 1,148,972 B, `schemaVersion: 3`.
- **`build_seed.py`:** 7.4 s cold (no `.thumb-cache.json`, 52 thumbnails via `sips`) vs 0.10 s
  warm — ~74×, replacing the draft contract's guessed "~80×". The cache is per-checkout, so a
  fresh worktree always pays cold.
- **Inline `const SEED`:** 129,136 chars after `embed_seed.py` strips 52 thumbnails, and it
  currently drifts from the library on **20 plan entries**.
- **Service-worker cache:** `mealplanner-v27`, precaching `index.html` + 16 files under
  `app/js/`. A clean app load emits **zero** console messages.
- **Sync outage:** 2026-08-01 08:52 → 2026-08-04 14:08 (three days, unnoticed).

gotchasMd:
# Meal Planner app — GOTCHAS

APPEND ONLY (use `tm gotcha "…" [--task ID]`). One bullet per trap, immediately on
discovery — not at end of session. Point at the knowledge/ file if one exists.
- (2026-08-02) app/sw.js precaches index.html AND every app/js/*.js under one `const CACHE`, but scripts/pre-commit only fires on app/index.html. A JS-only change commits clean and ships silently stale to installed phones. Bump CACHE by hand for any app/js/ edit.
- (2026-08-02) build_seed.py resolves the markdown library as ../.. from app/, which does NOT resolve from a git worktree. Set MP_BASE_DIR="/Users/rutgerboll/Documents/Claude/Projects/Meal planning" before running it from a worktree.
- (2026-08-04, T0.1) A listening port is not a working server. com.mealplanner.server held
8765 for days while returning 404 on every static path and 500 on /sync.json — the
LaunchAgent cannot read under ~/Documents without Full Disk Access for /usr/bin/python3.
SYNC-SETUP.md predicts a silent crash-loop; the real behaviour is worse, it stays up. Always
curl a real path. deploy.sh's health check is lsof LISTEN, so it prints the success tick over
exactly this failure. See knowledge/instruments.md. · rutgerboll@Rutgers-Mini#T0.1
- (2026-08-04, T0.1) app/seed.json is server-owned runtime output, not a source file that
someone forgot to commit. meal-server.py re-runs build_seed.py and rewrites it on every
/sync.json request, so the main checkout is permanently dirty and deploy.sh's
dirty-checkout guard refuses every time. A fresh build reproduces the uncommitted copy
byte-for-byte; HEAD's copy is the stale one. Never git add -A here. · rutgerboll@Rutgers-Mini#T0.1
- (2026-08-04, T0.1) build_seed.py does NOT refresh the inline `const SEED` in index.html —
embed_seed.py is a separate, easily-skipped step, and skipping it is currently live: the
committed bootstrap disagrees with the markdown library on 20 plan entries. Invisible while
the mini is up (the app auto-syncs on load), wrong-and-silent on a fresh install when it is
not. · rutgerboll@Rutgers-Mini#T0.1
- (2026-08-04, T0.1) CORRECTS the earlier T0.1 gotcha above that blamed Full Disk Access. The
404-behind-a-live-port outage was real, but the cause was NOT a missing FDA grant: an
accidental pkill killed the stuck process, launchd restarted it, and the fresh process serves
everything correctly under the same plist. Cause unknown. Two rules that do survive — curl a
real path before trusting any server (lsof LISTEN passes on a dead one), and stop your own
test server BY PID (kill $(lsof -ti :8766 -sTCP:LISTEN)), never pkill -f meal-server.py, which
takes the phone's server down with it. · rutgerboll@Rutgers-Mini#T0.1
